pointers.sentence: The flat pages application keeps the first in the database, one-off pages a project would not write an application for, in its documentation's words (`docs/ref/contrib/flatpages.txt`); the redirects application keeps the second.
One more field, `enable_comments`, is read by nothing in Django and shown by no fieldset of the admin; the documentation leaves it to a project (`django/contrib/flatpages/models.py:FlatPage`).
Site and old path are unique together (`django/contrib/redirects/models.py:Redirect`).
Both are class attributes, for a subclass to change, a comment says (`django/contrib/redirects/middleware.py:RedirectFallbackMiddleware`).

If it raises anything else, so does the 404, unless `settings.DEBUG` is true, when the exception goes on; the comment's reason is that a middleware cannot assume the error will be caught elsewhere (`django/contrib/flatpages/middleware.py:FlatpageFallbackMiddleware.process_response`).

`BaseHandler._get_response` calls the `process_view` hooks only after the URL resolves, so none has run for a path that resolves nowhere (`django/core/handlers/base.py:BaseHandler._get_response`) ([The centre of the chain](../handlers/view.md)).

`CommonMiddleware` would not: it adds a slash only when the path with one resolves in the URLconf, and the path of a flat page the middleware serves resolves nowhere ([Resolving a path](../urls/resolving.md#the-resolvers-other-callers)) (`django/contrib/flatpages/views.py:flatpage`).
The view gives the template one variable, "flatpage", and the request, so the context processors add theirs (`django/contrib/flatpages/views.py:render_flatpage`).

The documentation warns that Django does not sanitize a flat page's HTML, that a malicious page can lead to permission escalation, and that only trusted users should add or edit pages (`docs/ref/contrib/flatpages.txt`).
The flat pages application's URLconf is one pattern, `"<path:url>"` to `flatpage`, for a project to include under a prefix (`django/contrib/flatpages/urls.py`).

`FlatPage.get_absolute_url` reverses the view with the page's URL, without its leading slash and then with it; when neither reverses, it returns the URL after the script prefix, added by hand, a comment says, because it bypasses `reverse` (`django/contrib/flatpages/models.py:FlatPage.get_absolute_url`).
The documentation's catch-all is a regular expression that matches only a path ending in a slash (`docs/ref/contrib/flatpages.txt`); with it, /bulletins/1 was redirected again.

Its `url` field is a `RegexField` of letters, digits, dots, underscores, hyphens, slashes and tildes; `FlatpageForm.clean_url` requires a leading slash, and a trailing one when `settings.APPEND_SLASH` is true and `MIDDLEWARE` holds "django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware"; `FlatpageForm.clean` refuses a URL another page has on any of the chosen sites (`django/contrib/flatpages/forms.py:FlatpageForm`).
`FlatPageAdmin` uses the form, and puts `registration_required` and `template_name` in a collapsed fieldset of advanced options (`django/contrib/flatpages/admin.py:FlatPageAdmin`).
It never looks at the request's user (`django/contrib/flatpages/templatetags/flatpages.py:FlatpageNode.render`):

`FlatPageSitemap` lists for a sitemap the pages without `registration_required` of the site `SITE_ID` names, asking `SiteManager.get_current` without a request (`django/contrib/flatpages/sitemaps.py:FlatPageSitemap.items`) ([Sitemaps: `Sitemap` and the sitemap views](sitemaps.md)).
